name: Derm-grade skincare routine

lead: A derm-grade routine borrows the basics dermatologists describe: a gentle cleanser, daily sunscreen and, for some people, a night-time retinoid. The payoff is clearer, more even, smoother-looking skin and slower visible sun damage.

The American Academy of Dermatology's guidance for adults lists a cleanser morning and night, optional vitamin C in the morning, broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher, and a retinoid at night, with results judged after at least 30 days.

paras: The routine is built from a small number of products used consistently: cleanse, treat, apply sunscreen in the morning, and use a retinoid at night, adding a moisturizer if dryness appears. Courses and creators package this as a protocol.

Retinoids can cause dryness and irritation, and the AAD cautions against overusing exfoliants. Prescription retinoids and persistent conditions such as acne, eczema or rosacea are handled by a dermatologist.

web.title: Dermatologist-recommended skin care for your 20s - AAD

chain: Retinoid at night for tone and texture
More even, clearer-looking skin over weeks
angle.text: The routine targets visible skin features: sunscreen limits sun-related dark spots and aging, retinoids work on tone, texture and acne, and cleansing keeps skin clear.

lead: A derm-grade skincare routine is a regimen modelled on dermatologists' basic recommendations and promoted in some looksmaxxing courses as a way to improve skin quality. Skin is a large part of how a face reads, so even tone, texture and clarity matter alongside structure.

The American Academy of Dermatology describes a daily routine of cleansing morning and night, an optional vitamin C serum in the morning, broad-spectrum water-resistant sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, and a night-time retinoid applied after washing. For dryness it suggests a non-clogging moisturizer, and it advises sticking with a routine for at least 30 days before judging results.[1]
The same guidance advises removing makeup before bed, avoiding scrubbing and tanning beds, and being cautious with trending exfoliants.[1]

paras: Cleansers are matched to skin type: oil-removing for acne-prone skin and hydrating for dry skin. Sunscreen goes on after other morning products and under makeup. Over-the-counter retinol addresses uneven tone, dark spots and texture, while prescription retinoids and adapalene are used for acne.[1]
No studies found for the routine as a packaged protocol. Individual components such as sunscreen and retinoids have their own bodies of dermatological research.
